Principle 20: Famous Places to Visit in Korea
Geographical Location of Korea
Korea is a peninsula located between China and Japan and is surrounded by three seas: the East Sea, the West Sea, and the South Sea.
Its geographical landscape is beautiful and filled with many wonderful places to visit.
Famous Places to Visit in Korea
Korea has a great number of attractive places to visit.
Some places are naturally beautiful such as Sorak Mountain while others are more historically aesthetic such as Bulguk Temple.
There are still those that were skillfully manmade like Independence Hall.
Perhaps several of the more popular attractions to visit in Korea are the Korean Folk Village in Suwon, the historical capital of GyeongJu, and the breathtaking Jeju Island.
A Homemade Piece of History: The Korean Folk Village in Suwon
One very interesting place to visit is the Korean Folk Village located near the city of Suwon in Gyunggi Province, not far from the capital of Seoul.
When you visit there, you can witness a traditional wedding ceremony, taste a variety of traditional foods, and you can observe how Koreans lived during ancient times.
It is a very popular attraction for many foreign visitors.
A Piece of Korean History: GyeongJu
Another attractive destination is GyeongJu located in South GyeongSang Province.
GyeongJu is the old capital of the Shilla Kingdom.
The Shilla Kingdom unified the divided land of Korea from three kingdoms into one that was known as the Unified Shilla Kingdom.
The Shilla Kingdom was its most powerful during the eighth century.
Many people regard GyeongJu as a museum without walls.
Koreans refer to it as this because it contains many of the old remains of the Shilla Dynasty.
A Natural Wonder: Jeju Island
Perhaps the most famous natural wonder of Korea is an island called Jeju.
Jeju island is a favorite place amongst Korean newlyweds to go on their honeymoons.
There are so many fun things to do on Jeju Island and many beautiful spots to visit.
Mt. Halla is the most visible attraction on Jeju Island.
It is located in the center of Jeju Island and is the highest mountain in South Korea; it’s almost 2,000 meters high (about 6500 feet).
